title: Prior-season PDO gave no clear added winter forecast gain in a 1981-2025 linear test
abstract: We tested whether the previous winter PDO improved the next winter forecast beyond recent PDO and Nino 3.4. We used fixed NOAA ERSSTv5 index tables and separate winter and summer linear models. Each forecast used earlier target years only. There were 45 test years, 1981-2025, after training from 1952. Adding the previous winter index raised winter mean squared error from 0.572125 to 0.591728, an increase of 3.43%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -8.61% to +0.56%. Adding the previous summer index raised summer error by 2.41%. Winter minus summer skill was -1.02 percentage points, with interval -7.67 to +4.79. Rolling training, a time trend and richer ENSO controls gave negative winter point skill with intervals that included zero. These results give no clear added winter forecast benefit under the tested baseline. They do not establish that ocean heat storage is absent. Revised surface indices, 45 dependent test years, simple linear models and uncertainty conditional on saved forecasts limit inference. The package includes exact raw tables, hashes, code, all forecasts, block draws, a figure and a separate numerical audit.
